archetypes.name: awk-entity-artifacts
archetypes.rationale: The plan's awk code blocks contain HTML-entity-encoded operators (> for >, & for &&) that would produce broken awk if copied literally into the script.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect every code block in the plan for HTML-entity-encoded characters such as >, &, <, and ". These appear in the awk snippets proposed for scripts/test-implement-structure.sh and would produce awk patterns that never match anything if copied verbatim. Read the existing awk blocks in scripts/test-implement-structure.sh and compare them against the plan's proposed replacements to confirm whether operator symbols in the plan are valid shell/awk syntax or corrupted entities. Flag any snippet where the plan's literal bytes differ from the intended shell semantics. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: awk-export-flag-scope
archetypes.rationale: The plan adds a file-scoped 'exported' awk variable without specifying an FNR==1 reset; if the scanner invokes awk over multiple files in one call the flag bleeds across files and falsely satisfies the pin check.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read scripts/test-implement-structure.sh to determine whether the A1 scanner's awk is invoked once per file inside a shell loop or once across all files as multiple awk arguments. The plan introduces an 'exported' flag that must reset at the start of each new file; without an FNR==1 { exported=0 } rule a preceding file's export LARCH_TIMING_SKILL=implement line could satisfy the record-round check for a different unrelated file. Verify whether the plan's awk snippet includes this per-file reset clause, and whether the existing scanner invocation structure makes the reset necessary. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: part-b-grep-literal
archetypes.rationale: The Part B structural assertion uses grep -qF with a literal string that must byte-match what the diff actually writes to lint-fix-loop.sh; a variable-name or quoting mismatch would silently pass the assertion regardless of whether the pin exists.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read scripts/lint-fix-loop.sh and locate the run_codex() function's Codex launcher invocation near line 366 to confirm the exact variable name used at the dispatch site is LINT_FIX_LOOP_LAUNCH_CODEX_EXEC_SH and not a shorter or differently-cased variant. Check that the grep -qF literal pattern in the plan's Part B assertion block, including the quoted form "$LINT_FIX_LOOP_LAUNCH_CODEX_EXEC_SH" with surrounding whitespace, matches the bytes the diff would actually write. A fixed-string grep that is too narrow (missing indentation) or references a variable name that differs from the one in the script would pass even if the pin is absent. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
